answer: Anchor identity to a rotating public beacon: each epoch the beacon publishes an unpredictable seed, and an agent must complete a seed-bound proof of useful work before its votes count. A prism check then splits that work across independent verifiers, so a single operator cannot grade its own copies. Each new identity starts with near-zero weight and gains influence only through a ripple of successful, publicly audited tasks over many epochs. Creating a thousand copies means paying the beacon-bound work cost a thousand times, with no shortcut, while honest agents compound reputation once.
